assumptions: Customer's approved vendor list is Stripe and Plaid; hosts used are api.stripe.com and production.plaid.com, the ones in the workspace code
Cardholder data = card_number, card_cvv/cvc/cvv, pan, card_expiry, cardholder_name
Advisory enforcement is the right default; the customer decides whether to make them blocking
Removing storage (not table columns) from charge_POST is in scope; deleting columns is not
Recipe's one-policy-per-template rule followed, so five template policies plus one own policy
confusions: SKILL.md was longer than the first read showed; the catalogue section and rule authoring were needed, took several reads
Recipe says to create each template as its own policy and then one policy of your own; unclear whether a single combined policy is preferred for an audit-facing ask. Followed the recipe
Whether a Stripe or Plaid host should be exact host or a suffix like .stripe.com: skill example used .example.com form; chose exact hosts actually in code, which is narrower

outbound.vendor_allowlist with kinds empty: the doc says non-http kinds with no providers are reported as not yet reviewed; this will flag Resend, OpenAI, Anthropic and Xano-internal kinds, unclear how much noise to expect
xano policy parse output is the reformatted policy with no warnings; no way to tell a clean parse from a parse that silently dropped something without reading it
wished_for: A recipe or template variant for PCI card data that includes cardholder-name and expiry as forbidden, since the template list is card_number and CVV only
A check or example for debug.log/datadog.log on named input fields, not only $input root
Guidance on whether the vendor allowlist should use exact hosts or host suffixes for vendors like Stripe and Plaid that use several subdomains
Example of how to check a field's value is cardholder data at runtime is out of reach; a sentence in the skill would have saved time
why_confidence: Storage of card fields, logging of input and vendor hosts are each checked by a rule that names the relevant fields or hosts, and the dry run is clean. But the rules read definitions only: a runtime value moved through a variable, the remaining card fields on payments, and the unapproved fraud-check vendor are all reported findings that only resolve when the customer acts. No policy here can prove the audit requirements are met.
